subject.title: fix(telegram): scope dispatch dedupe by bot identity

question: Should Telegram upgrades intentionally ignore all legacy unscoped V1 dispatch-dedupe claims, accepting at most one V1-to-V2 redelivery in order to guarantee that reused state cannot suppress a different bot’s message?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but choosing between bounded duplicate delivery and backward use of an identity-ambiguous persisted claim is a message-delivery policy decision that cannot be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the V2 cutover
options.body: Keep V2-only claims and accept the bounded first-redelivery duplicate risk as the safer alternative to silent cross-bot suppression.

options.title: Require an explicit upgrade mechanism
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers define a safe migration or operator-visible transition policy for legacy V1 claims.

recommendation.title: Approve the V2 cutover
recommendation.body: Keep V2-only claims and accept the bounded first-redelivery duplicate risk as the safer alternative to silent cross-bot suppression.
